verses.text: Adam, Seth, Enosh,
Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared,
Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech,
Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
The sons of Japheth were: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.
The sons of Gomer were: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
The sons of Javan were: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.
The sons of Ham were: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan.
The sons of Cush were: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabteca. The sons of Raamah were: Sheba and Dedan.
Cush was the father of Nimrod, who became a mighty warrior on the earth.
Egypt was the father of the Ludites, the Anamites, the Lehabites, the Naphtuhites,
The Pathrusites, the Casluhites (from whom the Philistines came), and the Caphtorites.
Canaan was the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and of the Hittites,
The Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
The Hivites, the Arkites, the Sinites,
The Arvadites, the Zemarites, and the Hamathites.
The sons of Shem were: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. The sons of Aram were: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.
Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah was the father of Eber.
Two sons were born to Eber: one was named Peleg, because in his lifetime the earth was divided, and his brother was named Joktan.
Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,
Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,
Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,
Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were the sons of Joktan.
Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,
Eber, Peleg, Reu,
Serug, Nahor, Terah,
And Abram, who is Abraham.
The sons of Abraham were: Isaac and Ishmael.
These were their descendants: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,
Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were the sons of Ishmael.
The sons born to Keturah, Abraham's concubine, were: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan were: Sheba and Dedan.
The sons of Midian were: Ephah, Epher, Henoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the descendants of Keturah.
Abraham was the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac were: Esau and Israel.
The sons of Esau were: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.
The sons of Eliphaz were: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz; and by Timna, Eliphaz had Amalek.
The sons of Reuel were: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.
The sons of Seir were: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.
The sons of Lotan were: Hori and Homam. Timna was Lotan's sister.
The sons of Shobal were: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon were: Aiah and Anah.
The son of Anah was: Dishon. The sons of Dishon were: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.
The sons of Ezer were: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan were: Uz and Aran.
These were the kings who ruled in the land of Edom before any king ruled over the people of Israel: Bela son of Beor, whose city was named Dinhabah.
When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah, from Bozrah, ruled in his place.
When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites ruled in his place.
When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad ruled in his place. Hadad defeated Midian in the country of Moab. His city was named Avith.
When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah ruled in his place.
When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth on the river ruled in his place.
When Shaul died, Baal-Hanan son of Achbor ruled in his place.
When Baal-Hanan died, Hadad ruled in his place. His city was named Pai, and his wife's name was Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, daughter of Mezahab.
After Hadad died, the chiefs of Edom were: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,
Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon,
Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,
Magdiel, and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.

1.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter is a genealogical list; archaic constructions like 'begat' were modernized to 'was the father of,' and the archaic title 'duke' (Hebrew alluph, a tribal leader) was rendered 'chief.' Name spellings follow the more familiar forms used elsewhere in this project (e.g. 'Sidon' rather than 'Zidon') for consistency.

verses.text: These were the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,
Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The sons of Judah were: Er, Onan, and Shelah. These three were born to him by Bathshua, a Canaanite woman. Er, Judah's firstborn, was evil in the sight of the LORD, so the LORD put him to death.
Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bore him Perez and Zerah. Judah had five sons in all.
The sons of Perez were: Hezron and Hamul.
The sons of Zerah were: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda — five in all.
The son of Carmi was: Achar, who brought trouble on Israel by taking what was set apart for destruction.
The son of Ethan was: Azariah.
The sons born to Hezron were: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Caleb.
Ram was the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab was the father of Nahshon, a leader of the people of Judah.
Nahshon was the father of Salmon, and Salmon was the father of Boaz,
Boaz was the father of Obed, and Obed was the father of Jesse,
And Jesse was the father of his firstborn Eliab, Abinadab the second son, Shimea the third,
Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth,
Ozem the sixth, and David the seventh.
Their sisters were Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah were three: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel.
Abigail was the mother of Amasa, whose father was Jether the Ishmaelite.
Caleb son of Hezron had children by his wife Azubah, and by Jerioth. Her sons were: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
When Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, who bore him Hur.
Hur was the father of Uri, and Uri was the father of Bezalel.
Later, Hezron slept with the daughter of Makir, the father of Gilead, whom he married when he was sixty years old. She bore him Segub.
Segub was the father of Jair, who ruled twenty-three towns in the land of Gilead.
But Geshur and Aram captured the towns of Jair, along with Kenath and its sixty surrounding villages. All these belonged to the descendants of Makir, the father of Gilead.
After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, Abijah, Hezron's wife, bore him Ashhur, the father of Tekoa.
The sons of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron, were: Ram his firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.
Jerahmeel had another wife named Atarah, who was the mother of Onam.
The sons of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, were: Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.
The sons of Onam were: Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai were: Nadab and Abishur.
Abishur's wife was named Abihail, and she bore him Ahban and Molid.
The sons of Nadab were: Seled and Appaim. Seled died without children.
The son of Appaim was: Ishi. The son of Ishi was: Sheshan. The child of Sheshan was: Ahlai.
The sons of Jada, Shammai's brother, were: Jether and Jonathan. Jether died without children.
The sons of Jonathan were: Peleth and Zaza. These were the descendants of Jerahmeel.
Sheshan had no sons, only daughters. Sheshan had an Egyptian servant named Jarha.
Sheshan gave his daughter in marriage to his servant Jarha, and she bore him Attai.
Attai was the father of Nathan, and Nathan was the father of Zabad,
Zabad was the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal was the father of Obed,
Obed was the father of Jehu, and Jehu was the father of Azariah,
Azariah was the father of Helez, and Helez was the father of Eleasah,
Eleasah was the father of Sismai, and Sismai was the father of Shallum,
Shallum was the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah was the father of Elishama.
The sons of Caleb, Jerahmeel's brother, were: Mesha his firstborn, who was the father of Ziph, and the descendants of Mareshah, the father of Hebron.
The sons of Hebron were: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.
Shema was the father of Raham, the father of Jorkoam. Rekem was the father of Shammai.
The son of Shammai was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.
Ephah, Caleb's concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran was the father of Gazez.
The sons of Jahdai were: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.
Maakah, Caleb's concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah.
She also bore Shaaph, the father of Madmannah, and Sheva, the father of Makbenah and Gibea. Caleb's daughter was Aksah.
These were the descendants of Caleb. The sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, were: Shobal, the father of Kiriath Jearim,
Salma, the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph, the father of Beth Gader.
Shobal, the father of Kiriath Jearim, had sons: Haroeh, and half of the clan of Manahath.
The clans of Kiriath Jearim were: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites. From them came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites.
The sons of Salma were: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, half of the Manahathites, and the Zorites.
And the clans of scribes who lived at Jabez were: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These were the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rekab.

2.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter is a genealogical list tracing Judah's line to David; 'begat' modernized to 'was the father of' throughout.

verses.text: These were the sons born to David in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, by Ahinoam of Jezreel; the second, Daniel, by Abigail of Carmel;
The third, Absalom, whose mother was Maakah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah, whose mother was Haggith;
The fifth, Shephatiah, whose mother was Abital; the sixth, Ithream, by his wife Eglah.
These six were born to him in Hebron, where David ruled for seven years and six months. He ruled in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
These were the sons born to him in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon — four of them by Bathsheba, daughter of Ammiel.
There were also Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet,
Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia,
Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet — nine in all.
These were all the sons of David, not counting the sons of his concubines, and their sister Tamar.
Solomon's son was Rehoboam; his son was Abijah; his son was Asa; his son was Jehoshaphat;
His son was Joram; his son was Ahaziah; his son was Joash;
His son was Amaziah; his son was Azariah; his son was Jotham;
His son was Ahaz; his son was Hezekiah; his son was Manasseh;
His son was Amon; his son was Josiah.
The sons of Josiah were: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, and the fourth Shallum.
The successors of Jehoiakim were: his son Jeconiah, and his son Zedekiah.
The sons of Jeconiah, who was taken captive, were: Shealtiel,
Malkiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.
The sons of Pedaiah were: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel were: Meshullam and Hananiah, and their sister Shelomith.
There were also Hashubah, Ohel, Berekiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed — five in all.
The sons of Hananiah were: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. The descendants continued through Rephaiah, Arnan, Obadiah, and Shekaniah.
The son of Shekaniah was: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah were: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat — six in all.
The sons of Neariah were: Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam — three in all.
The sons of Elioenai were: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani — seven in all.

3.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter traces David's descendants and the line of the kings of Judah down through the Babylonian exile.

verses.text: The sons of Judah were: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.
Reaiah son of Shobal was the father of Jahath, and Jahath was the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These were the clans of the Zorathites.
These were the sons of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was named Hazzelelponi.
Penuel was the father of Gedor, and Ezer was the father of Hushah. These were the descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah and father of Bethlehem.
Ashhur, the father of Tekoa, had two wives, Helah and Naarah.
Naarah bore him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These were the sons of Naarah.
The sons of Helah were: Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan.
Koz was the father of Anub and Zobebah, and of the clans of Aharhel son of Harum.
Jabez was more honored than his brothers. His mother named him Jabez, saying, I bore him in pain.

Jabez called out to the God of Israel: If only you would bless me and expand my territory! Let your hand be with me, and keep me from harm, so that I will be free from pain. And God granted his request.
Kelub, the brother of Shuhah, was the father of Mehir, who was the father of Eshton.
Eshton was the father of Beth-Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, the father of Ir-Nahash. These were the men of Rekah.
The sons of Kenaz were: Othniel and Seraiah. The son of Othniel was: Hathath.
Meonothai was the father of Ophrah. Seraiah was the father of Joab, the father of Ge Harashim — so called because its people were craftsmen.
The sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh were: Iru, Elah, and Naam. The son of Elah was: Kenaz.
The sons of Jehallelel were: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.
The sons of Ezrah were: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. One of Mered's wives gave birth to Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah, the father of Eshtemoa.

(His wife from Judah gave birth to Jered, the father of Gedor, Heber, the father of Soko, and Jekuthiel, the father of Zanoah.) These were the sons of Bithiah, daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered had married.
The sons of the wife of Hodiah, sister of Naham, were: the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maakathite.
The sons of Shimon were: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi were: Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.
The sons of Shelah son of Judah were: Er, the father of Lekah, Laadah, the father of Mareshah, and the clans of the linen workers at Beth Ashbea,
Jokim, the men of Kozeba, and Joash and Saraph, who ruled in Moab before returning to Bethlehem. (These records are old.)
These were the potters who lived in Netaim and Gederah. They lived there and worked for the king.
The sons of Simeon were: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.
Shallum was Shaul's son, Mibsam was his son, and Mishma was his son.
The descendants of Mishma were: his son Hammuel, his son Zaccur, and his son Shimei.
Shimei had sixteen sons and six daughters, but his brothers did not have many children, so the whole clan did not grow as large as the people of Judah.
They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, Hazar Shual,
Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,
Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,
Beth Markaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim. These were their towns until the time David became king.
Their villages were: Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Token, and Ashan — five towns,
Along with all the villages around these towns, as far as Baalath. This was where they lived, and this was their family record.
Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah son of Amaziah,
Joel, Jehu son of Joshibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel,
Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, Benaiah,
And Ziza son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah —
These men listed by name were leaders of their clans. Their families grew greatly in number.
They went to the entrance of Gedor, to the east side of the valley, to look for pasture for their flocks.
They found rich, good pasture, and the land was wide, quiet, and peaceful. The people who had lived there before were descendants of Ham.

The men listed here, during the reign of King Hezekiah of Judah, came and destroyed the homes of those people, and the Meunites who were found there, wiping them out completely to this day. They settled in their place, because there was pasture there for their flocks.
Some of the Simeonites, five hundred men, went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi.
They destroyed the remaining Amalekites who had escaped, and they have lived there to this day.

4.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter continues Judah's genealogy (including the well-known Prayer of Jabez, v9-10) and covers the genealogy of Simeon.

verses.text: These were the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel. (Reuben was the firstborn, but because he dishonored his father's bed, his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph son of Israel. Reuben's descendants are not listed as the firstborn in the family records.
Judah became stronger than his brothers, and the ruler came from his line, but the birthright itself belonged to Joseph.)
So the sons of Reuben, the firstborn of Israel, were: Hanok, Pallu, Hezron, and Karmi.
The descendants of Joel were: his son Shemaiah, his son Gog, his son Shimei,
His son Micah, his son Reaiah, his son Baal,
And his son Beerah, whom Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria took into exile. Beerah was a leader of the Reubenites.
His relatives, listed by clan according to their family records, were: Jeiel the chief, then Zechariah,
And Bela son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel. They lived in Aroer, as far as Nebo and Baal Meon.
To the east they settled all the way to the edge of the desert that stretches to the Euphrates River, because their livestock had grown very numerous in the land of Gilead.
During the time of Saul, they fought against the Hagrites and defeated them. They settled in the Hagrites' tents throughout the eastern side of Gilead.
The people of Gad lived next to them in the land of Bashan, as far as Salekah.
Joel was the chief in Bashan, Shapham was next, then Janai, and Shaphat.
Their relatives, listed by families, were: Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jakan, Zia, and Eber — seven in all.
These were the descendants of Abihail son of Huri, son of Jaroah, son of Gilead, son of Michael, son of Jeshishai, son of Jahdo, son of Buz.
Ahi son of Abdiel, son of Guni, was the head of their family.
They lived in Gilead, in Bashan and its villages, and throughout the pasturelands of Sharon as far as their borders reached.
All these were listed in the family records during the reign of Jotham king of Judah and Jeroboam king of Israel.

The men of Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, who were brave warriors able to carry shield and sword, skilled with the bow, and trained for war, numbered forty-four thousand seven hundred sixty ready to go to battle.
They fought against the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

They received help against them, and the Hagrites and all their allies were handed over to them, because they cried out to God during the battle. God answered their prayer, because they trusted in him.
They captured the livestock of the Hagrites — fifty thousand camels, two hundred fifty thousand sheep, two thousand donkeys — and took a hundred thousand people captive.
Many were killed, because the battle belonged to God. They settled in the land in place of the Hagrites until the exile.
The people of the half-tribe of Manasseh lived in the land from Bashan to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon. They were very numerous.
These were the heads of their families: Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel — brave warriors, famous men, and heads of their families.
But they were unfaithful to the God of their ancestors and worshiped the gods of the peoples God had destroyed before them.

So the God of Israel stirred up King Pul of Assyria, that is, King Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria, and he took the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile. He brought them to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan, where they are to this day.

5.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter covers the genealogy of the Transjordan tribes -- Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh -- and their eventual exile.

verses.text: Levi's sons were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Amram's children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Eleazar was the father of Phinehas, and Phinehas was the father of Abishua,
Abishua was the father of Bukki, and Bukki was the father of Uzzi,
Uzzi was the father of Zerahiah, and Zerahiah was the father of Meraioth,
Meraioth was the father of Amariah, and Amariah was the father of Ahitub,
Ahitub was the father of Zadok, and Zadok was the father of Ahimaaz,
Ahimaaz was the father of Azariah, and Azariah was the father of Johanan,
Johanan was the father of Azariah. This Azariah served as priest in the temple that Solomon built in Jerusalem.
Azariah was the father of Amariah, and Amariah was the father of Ahitub,
Ahitub was the father of Zadok, and Zadok was the father of Shallum,
Shallum was the father of Hilkiah, and Hilkiah was the father of Azariah,
Azariah was the father of Seraiah, and Seraiah was the father of Jehozadak,
Jehozadak went into captivity when the LORD sent Judah and Jerusalem into exile through Nebuchadnezzar.
Levi's sons were Gershom, Kohath, and Merari.
Gershom's sons were named Libni and Shimei.
Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. These were the Levite families, listed by their fathers.
Gershom's line: Gershom was the father of Libni. Libni was the father of Jahath. Jahath was the father of Zimmah.
Zimmah was the father of Joah. Joah was the father of Iddo. Iddo was the father of Zerah. Zerah was the father of Jeaterai.
Kohath's line: Kohath was the father of Amminadab. Amminadab was the father of Korah. Korah was the father of Assir.
Assir was the father of Elkanah. Elkanah was the father of Ebiasaph. Ebiasaph was the father of Assir.
That Assir was the father of Tahath. Tahath was the father of Uriel. Uriel was the father of Uzziah. Uzziah was the father of Shaul.
Elkanah's sons were Amasai and Ahimoth.
As for the family of Elkanah: Elkanah was the father of Zophai, and Zophai was the father of Nahath,
Nahath was the father of Eliab. Eliab was the father of Jeroham. Jeroham was the father of Elkanah.
Samuel's sons were Joel the firstborn and Abijah the second son.
Merari's line: Merari's son was Mahli. Mahli's son was Libni. Libni's son was Shimei. Shimei's son was Uzza.
Uzza's son was Shimea. Shimea's son was Haggiah. Haggiah's son was Asaiah.
These were the men David appointed to lead the music in the house of the LORD, after the ark of the covenant came to rest there.
They served with singing in front of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, until Solomon built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem. Then they carried out their duties in the order assigned to them.
These were the men who served, along with their sons. From the family of Kohath: Heman the singer, son of Joel, son of Shemuel,
son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,
son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,
son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,
son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,
son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.
Heman's relative Asaph stood at Heman's right hand. Asaph was the son of Berachiah, son of Shimea,
son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchiah,
son of Ethni, son of Zerah, son of Adaiah,
son of Ethan, son of Zimmah, son of Shimei,
son of Jahath, son of Gershom, son of Levi.
Their relatives of the family of Merari stood at the left hand: Ethan son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,
son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,
son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shamer,
son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.
The rest of their fellow Levites were appointed to all the other work of the tabernacle, the house of God.

But Aaron and Aaron's sons offered sacrifices on the altar of burnt offering and on the altar of incense. They were appointed to do all the work of the most holy place and to make atonement for Israel, exactly as Moses, the servant of God, had commanded.
Now here again is the line of Aaron: Aaron's son was Eleazar. Eleazar's son was Phinehas. Phinehas's son was Abishua.
Abishua's son was Bukki. Bukki's son was Uzzi. Uzzi's son was Zerahiah.
Zerahiah's son was Meraioth. Meraioth's son was Amariah. Amariah's son was Ahitub.
Ahitub's son was Zadok. Zadok's son was Ahimaaz.
Now these were the places where Aaron's descendants lived, within their territories and settlements — the Kohathite families, since the first lot fell to them.
The people of Israel gave them Hebron in the land of Judah, along with the pasturelands around it.
But the open fields and villages around the city were given to Caleb son of Jephunneh.
To the descendants of Aaron they gave these cities of Judah: Hebron, a city of refuge, and Libnah with its pasturelands, and Jattir and Eshtemoa with their pasturelands,
and Hilen with its pasturelands, and Debir with its pasturelands,
and Ashan with its pasturelands, and Bethshemesh with its pasturelands.

From the tribe of Benjamin they were given Geba with its pasturelands, Alemeth with its pasturelands, and Anathoth with its pasturelands. In all, the families of Aaron's descendants received thirteen cities.
The rest of Kohath's descendants, from the remaining Kohathite families, were given ten cities by lot from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Gershom's descendants, by their families, received thirteen cities from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
Merari's descendants, by their families, were given twelve cities by lot from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
So the people of Israel gave the Levites these cities, along with their pasturelands.
They gave by lot, from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin, the cities already named above.
The rest of the Kohathite families received cities from the territory of the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, a city of refuge, with its pasturelands, and also Gezer with its pasturelands,
and Jokmeam with its pasturelands, and Bethhoron with its pasturelands,
and Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gathrimmon with its pasturelands.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh, the rest of the Kohathite family received Aner with its pasturelands and Bileam with its pasturelands.
Gershom's descendants were given, from the half-tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan with its pasturelands, and Ashtaroth with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Issachar they received Kedesh with its pasturelands, and Daberath with its pasturelands,
and Ramoth with its pasturelands, and Anem with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Asher they received Mashal with its pasturelands, and Abdon with its pasturelands,
and Hukok with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Naphtali they received Kedesh in Galilee with its pasturelands, Hammon with its pasturelands, and Kirjathaim with its pasturelands.
The rest of Merari's descendants were given, from the tribe of Zebulun, Rimmon with its pasturelands and Tabor with its pasturelands.

On the other side of the Jordan from Jericho, on the east side of the Jordan, they were given, from the tribe of Reuben, Bezer in the wilderness with its pasturelands, and Jahzah with its pasturelands,
and Kedemoth with its pasturelands, and Mephaath with its pasturelands.
From the tribe of Gad they received Ramoth in Gilead with its pasturelands, and Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
and Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands.

6.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter covers the Levite genealogy (the priestly line through Aaron, and the three Levite clans of Gershom, Kohath, and Merari), David's temple musicians, and the Levitical cities. V10 and v39 name referents that were bare pronouns in the KJV ('he'/'his brother'); v28 restores 'Joel' as Samuel's firstborn, following 1 Samuel 8:2 and the near-universal scholarly reading that KJV's 'Vashni' is a scribal corruption of the Hebrew for 'and the second' with the firstborn's actual name having dropped out; 'Gershon' (KJV's spelling in v1 only) was standardized to 'Gershom,' used elsewhere throughout this chapter and the rest of the book; and KJV's 'suburbs' (Hebrew migrash, open common land around a city) was rendered 'pasturelands' throughout, since 'suburbs' now means something quite different.

verses.text: The sons of Issachar were: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron — four in all.

The sons of Tola were: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam, and Shemuel — heads of their families, descended from Tola. They were brave warriors, and in the time of David they numbered twenty-two thousand six hundred.
The son of Uzzi was: Izrahiah. The sons of Izrahiah were: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah — five in all, all of them leaders.
With them, listed by their families, were military units numbering thirty-six thousand men, because they had many wives and children.
Their relatives throughout all the clans of Issachar were brave warriors; all of them listed in the family records numbered eighty-seven thousand.
The sons of Benjamin were: Bela, Beker, and Jediael — three in all.
The sons of Bela were: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri — five in all, heads of their families, brave warriors, and listed in the family records as twenty-two thousand thirty-four.
The sons of Beker were: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Beker.
Listed by their family records, the heads of their families and brave warriors numbered twenty thousand two hundred.
The son of Jediael was: Bilhan. The sons of Bilhan were: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Kenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
All these sons of Jediael, heads of their families, were brave warriors, seventeen thousand two hundred ready to serve in battle.
Shuppim and Huppim were sons of Ir. Hushim was the son of Aher.
The sons of Naphtali were: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum — descendants of Bilhah.
The son of Manasseh through his Aramean concubine was: Asriel. She also bore Makir, the father of Gilead.
Makir found wives for Huppim and Shuppim. His sister's name was Maakah. The second son was named Zelophehad, and Zelophehad had only daughters.
Maakah, the wife of Makir, gave birth to a son and named him Peresh. His brother was named Sheresh, and Sheresh's sons were Ulam and Rekem.
The son of Ulam was: Bedan. These were the descendants of Gilead son of Makir, son of Manasseh.
His sister Hammoleketh gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
The sons of Shemida were: Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.
The descendants of Ephraim were: Shuthelah, his son Bered, his son Tahath, his son Eleadah, his son Tahath,
His son Zabad, his son Shuthelah, and also Ezer and Elead, who were killed by the men of Gath, natives of that land, because they came down to steal their livestock.
Their father Ephraim mourned for them many days, and his relatives came to comfort him.
Then he slept with his wife, and she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Ephraim named him Beriah, because tragedy had struck his family.
(His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth Horon, and also Uzzen Sheerah.)
His son was Rephah, then Resheph, then Telah, then Tahan,
Then Ladan, then Ammihud, then Elishama,
Then Nun, then Joshua.
Their lands and settlements included Bethel and its villages, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its villages to the west, and Shechem and its villages, as far as Ayyah and its villages.

Along the borders of Manasseh were Beth Shean and its villages, Taanach and its villages, Megiddo and its villages, and Dor and its villages. The descendants of Joseph son of Israel lived in these places.
The sons of Asher were: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister was Serah.
The sons of Beriah were: Heber and Malkiel, who was the father of Birzaith.
Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham, and their sister Shua.
The sons of Japhlet were: Pasak, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were the sons of Japhlet.
The sons of Shemer were: Ahi, Rohgah, Hubbah, and Aram.
The sons of his brother Helem were: Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
The sons of Zophah were: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,
Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran, and Beera.
The sons of Jether were: Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.
The sons of Ulla were: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.

All these were descendants of Asher, heads of their families, chosen men, brave warriors, and leaders among the princes. Listed in the family records as fit for military service, they numbered twenty-six thousand.

7.source: Drafted from the public-domain King James Version, checked verse-by-verse against the Hebrew text (Strong's Concordance / Blue Letter Bible) for word accuracy. This chapter covers the genealogies of Issachar, Benjamin, Naphtali, Manasseh, Ephraim (including the deaths of Ezer and Elead in a cattle raid, v21-23), and Asher.
